mainTopic: Which measurements of the מזבח in יחזקאל's פסוק use the small five-handbreadth cubit, tested against the red line, the משנה in מדות, and the size of the עזרה.
overview: The גמרא finishes a פסוק in יחזקאל about the מזבח and matches each phrase to a part of it: the יסוד, the סובב, the קרנות, and the מזבח הזהב. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה both learn from the word 'זה'. רבי מאיר says only the מזבח הזהב uses the small five-handbreadth cubit, and רבי יהודה says all the כלים do. The גמרא then asks which measurements of the outer מזבח use the small cubit. A first idea, that the height from the יסוד to the סובב uses small cubits, fails. It would put the blood of an עולת העוף below the red line. A second idea, that the three insets (כניסה) use small cubits, fixes the height. But it clashes with the round widths in the משנה in מדות, and 'לא דק' cannot explain the 24 by 24 area of the מערכה, which a פסוק fixes exactly. Saying that six of the base's cubits were short also fails, because the courtyard's 187 cubits would no longer add up. So the גמרא begins a new reading: 'חיק האמה' is the height of the יסוד and 'אמה רחב' is an inset, and the reading continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Explaining each phrase of the altar verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the פסוק from יחזקאל and matches each phrase to a part of the מזבח: the יסוד, the סובב, the קרנות, and מזבח הזהב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the bottom shall be a cubit, and the breadth a cubit, and its border by its edge round about shall be the one span, and this shall be the higher part of the altar.' 'The bottom a cubit' means the base. 'The breadth a cubit' means the surrounding ledge. 'Its border by its edge round about, one span' means the corners. 'This shall be the higher part of the altar' means the golden altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the פסוק in יחזקאל and explains which part of the מזבח each phrase is describing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first phrases describe the outer מזבח from the bottom up: the יסוד, then the סובב, then the קרנות. The last phrase, 'וזה גב המזבח', is read as moving to a different altar, the מזבח הזהב. That last phrase is what the next step's מחלוקת is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: The base of the outer מזבח, its lowest section
The ledge that runs around the middle of the outer מזבח
The raised corners on top of the מזבח
The golden altar inside the היכל, used for the קטורת
A span, about half a cubit

phrases.english: and the bottom shall be a cubit, and the breadth a cubit,
and its border by its edge round about
shall be the one span,
and this shall be the higher part of the altar.
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 43:13. The start of this פסוק was quoted just before this point.

phrases.english: 'The bottom a cubit' – this is the base;
'the breadth a cubit' – this is the surrounding ledge;

phrases.aramaic: ״וּגְבוּלָהּ אֶל שְׂפָתָהּ סָבִיב זֶרֶת הָאֶחָד״ – אֵלּוּ קְרָנוֹת,
phrases.english: 'and its border by its edge round about, the one span' – these are the corners;
'this shall be the higher part of the altar' – this is the golden altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation and explanation of the פסוק that the sugya brought just before this point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each phrase of the פסוק matches a part of the מזבח, and 'וזה גב המזבח' refers to the מזבח הזהב.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה read 'this' differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads 'זה' as limiting: only the golden altar uses a five-handbreadth cubit, and all other כלים use six. רבי יהודה reads 'זה' as a model: all the כלים use the five-handbreadth cubit, like this one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds that 'this' means only this one, the golden altar, is measured with a cubit of five handbreadths, but all the cubits of the other vessels use a cubit of six. רבי יהודה holds that 'this' means all the cubits of the vessels should be like this one.
steps.whatsHappening: Both תנאים learn from the same word 'זה', but they reach opposite results about which cubit is used to measure the כלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, 'זה' excludes: only the מזבח הזהב gets the small cubit. For רבי יהודה, 'זה' sets an example: every כלי is measured like the מזבח הזהב, with the small cubit. One word in the פסוק is read once as a limit and once as a pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: A small cubit of five handbreadths (טפחים)
A standard cubit of six handbreadths
The cubits used to measure the vessels of the מקדש
'This is it', read as limiting: only this one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: only the מזבח הזהב uses the five-handbreadth cubit. רבי יהודה: all the כלים use the five-handbreadth cubit.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sages agree that the מזבח הזהב is measured with five-handbreadth cubits. They only argue about the other כלים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: ״זֶהוּ״ – בְּאַמָּה בַּת חֲמִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds: 'This is it' – with a cubit of five handbreadths,
phrases.notes: He reads the word 'this' as 'only this one'.

phrases.aramaic: הָא כׇּל אַמּוֹת כֵּלִים בְּאַמָּה בַּת שֵׁשׁ.
phrases.english: but all the cubits of the vessels are with a cubit of six.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
Like this shall be all the cubits of the vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר זֶהוּ בְּאַמָּה בַּת חֲמִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the last phrase explained in step 1, 'וזה גב המזבח', as the source for both opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: only the מזבח הזהב uses the five-handbreadth cubit. רבי יהודה: all the כלים use the five-handbreadth cubit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains where each side of the מחלוקת about the size of the כלים' cubits comes from.

steps.title: A first suggestion: the base to the ledge uses small cubits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reading 'חיק האמה ואמה רחב' as saying that the height from the יסוד up to the סובב is measured in five-handbreadth cubits.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that from the base to the surrounding ledge, the height is measured with a cubit of five handbreadths. And what does 'the bottom a cubit and the breadth a cubit' mean? It is saying: from the cubit at the bottom up to the cubit of the breadth, use a cubit of five handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts forward a possible first reading of the פסוק. This step sets up the test that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this suggestion, the words 'חיק האמה ואמה רחב' mark the two ends of a stretch of height: from the יסוד to the סובב. That whole stretch would be measured with the small cubit. The phrase 'קא סלקא דעתך' tells us this is only a first thought, which the גמרא is about to check.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It enters your mind' – a first idea that may later be rejected
Height
'This is what it is saying' – introduces an explanation of the words

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say
that from the base until the surrounding ledge
the height is measured with a cubit of five handbreadths.
And what is the meaning of 'the bottom a cubit and the breadth a cubit'?
This is what it is saying:
from the cubit of the bottom until the cubit of the breadth
phrases.notes: In other words, from the יסוד up to the סובב.

phrases.english: is measured with a cubit of five handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ מִיְּסוֹד וְעַד סוֹבֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פסוק from step 1 and offers a first idea about which heights use the small cubit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A first suggestion: the height from the יסוד to the סובב is measured in five-handbreadth cubits.

steps.title: Working out the altar's height under this suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא checks the suggestion by adding up the height of the מזבח: ten cubits, with six of them at five handbreadths each and four of them at six handbreadths each.
steps.simpleTranslation: How tall is the altar? Ten cubits: six of them are five handbreadths each, and four of them are six handbreadths each.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to test the suggestion from step 3 by working out the full height of the מזבח in handbreadths. This sets up a problem that the גמרא presses next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stretch up to the סובב is six small cubits (6 × 5 = 30 טפחים) and the remaining four are regular cubits (4 × 6 = 24 טפחים), the total comes to 54 טפחים. The גמרא lays out this mixed calculation so it can examine whether this result holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten cubits, the height of the outer מזבח
Cubits of five handbreadths each
Cubits of six handbreadths each

phrases.english: The height of the altar, how much is it?
Ten cubits:
six of five handbreadths each,
phrases.notes: These six are the cubits from the ground up to the סובב: 30 handbreadths.

phrases.english: and four of six handbreadths each.
phrases.notes: These four go from the סובב to the top of the corners: 24 handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the suggestion from step 3 by working out its result for the total height.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the height from the יסוד to the סובב is measured in five-handbreadth cubits.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following the suggestion leads to a mixed total of six small cubits and four regular cubits. The גמרא sets out this result so it can examine whether it works, and continues pressing the problem next.

steps.title: Adding up the altar's height and finding the middle
steps.stepSummary: Under the suggested reading, the מזבח is 54 handbreadths tall, so its middle is at 27. The סובב is 24 handbreadths below the top, which puts it only 3 handbreadths above the middle. The red line runs around that middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: How tall is the altar? Fifty-four. Half the altar is how much? Twenty-seven. From the horns down to the ledge is how much? Twenty-four. How much short of half the altar is that? Three. And we learned: a red line goes around the middle of the altar, to separate the upper bloods from the lower bloods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the math it started in the last step. It shows that, on this reading, the סובב is just 3 handbreadths above the middle of the מזבח. This sets up the attack that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six cubits of 5 handbreadths (30) plus four cubits of 6 handbreadths (24) make 54, so the middle is at 27. The top 24 handbreadths sit above the סובב, so the סובב is at height 30, only 3 above the middle. The red line from the משנה marks that middle, and it splits blood that goes on top from blood that goes on the bottom.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of it (here, half the height of the מזבח)
Less than, short of
A red line painted around the middle of the מזבח
Blood that must be put on the upper half of the מזבח
Blood that must be put on the lower half of the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: "Short of half by three" means the top section (24) is 3 less than half (27). That puts the סובב 3 handbreadths ABOVE the middle, not below it.

phrases.english: How much is the altar's height? Fifty-four handbreadths.

phrases.aramaic: פַּלְגֵיהּ דְּמִזְבֵּחַ כַּמָּה הָוֵי? עֶשְׂרִין וְשִׁבְעָה.
phrases.english: Half of the altar is how much? Twenty-seven.

phrases.aramaic: מִקְּרָנוֹת וְעַד סוֹבֵב כַּמָּה הָוֵי? עֶשְׂרִין וְאַרְבְּעָה.
phrases.english: From the horns down to the ledge is how much? Twenty-four.
How much less than half the altar is that? Three.

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: חוּט שֶׁל סִקְרָא חוֹגְרוֹ בָּאֶמְצַע,
phrases.english: And we learned: a red line goes around it in the middle,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין דָּמִים הָעֶלְיוֹנִים לְדָמִים הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים.
phrases.english: to separate between the upper bloods and the lower bloods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the height calculation begun in step 4 and places the סובב relative to the red line.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading from step 3 that the פסוק describes heights measured in five-handbreadth cubits.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gathers the numbers (סובב only 3 handbreadths above the middle red line) that the next step uses to show a contradiction.

steps.title: The bird offering's blood would end up below the red line
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the כהן squeezes the blood of an עולת העוף while standing on the סובב, and it is still valid even one cubit below his feet. But one cubit (5 handbreadths) below a סובב that is only 3 above the middle lands 2 handbreadths below the middle. That puts upper blood on the lower half.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what was taught about the bird burnt offering: He would go up the ramp, turn to the ledge, and come to the southeast corner. He would pinch off its head from the back of its neck, separate it, and squeeze its blood onto the wall of the altar. And if he did it below his feet, even one cubit, it is valid. But then he is putting upper blood two handbreadths below the middle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the עולת העוף to attack the height reading. On that reading, the ברייתא would allow upper blood to be put below the red line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of an עולת העוף belongs on the upper half of the מזבח. The ברייתא allows squeezing it as much as one cubit below the סובב. With the סובב at 3 handbreadths above the middle, a 5-handbreadth cubit lower is 2 handbreadths below the middle, so the ברייתא could not call it כשירה. The suggested reading must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a burnt offering; its blood goes on the upper half of the מזבח
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Pinches off the bird's head with the fingernail (מליקה)
Squeezes out the blood against the wall (מיצוי)
Valid

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule about upper and lower blood is used as a hard test for how the מזבח was built.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא גַּבֵּי עוֹלַת הָעוֹף:
phrases.english: But then, what about that which was taught regarding the bird burnt offering:
He would go up the ramp and turn onto the ledge,
and come to the southeast corner,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, "east," is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹלֵק אֶת רֹאשָׁהּ מִמּוּל עׇרְפָּה, וּמַבְדִּיל,
phrases.english: and pinch off its head from opposite its nape, and separate it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹצֶה אֶת דָּמָהּ עַל קִיר הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: and squeeze its blood onto the wall of the altar,
and if he did it below his feet,
phrases.notes: His feet are on the סובב, so this means below the ledge.

phrases.english: even one cubit lower, it is valid.

phrases.aramaic: הָא קָא יָהֵיב עֶלְיוֹנָה לְמַטָּה מִשְּׁנֵי טְפָחִים!
phrases.english: But then he is placing upper blood two handbreadths below the middle!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא גַּבֵּי עוֹלַת הָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the numbers from step 5 to show a contradiction with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'חיק האמה ואמה רחב' measures height from the יסוד to the סובב in five-handbreadth cubits.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On that reading, the ברייתא would validate upper blood placed 2 handbreadths below the red line, which cannot be right.

steps.title: The verse describes setbacks, not heights
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the פסוק: each of the three phrases describes a one-cubit inset (כניסה) of the מזבח. The wall steps in at the יסוד, at the סובב, and at the horns. These five-handbreadth cubits measure width, not height.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: "the bottom a cubit" is an inset; "a cubit wide" is an inset; "its border by its edge all around" is an inset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the height reading and gives a new one. The three phrases of the פסוק describe how far the מזבח steps inward at each level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The height reading failed because of the עולת העוף ברייתא. Now the five-handbreadth cubits measure how far the wall steps in: one cubit above the יסוד, one cubit at the סובב, and one cubit for the horns. Since nothing here affects the heights, the problem with the red line disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: An inset or setback, where the wall of the מזבח steps inward
"The bottom, a cubit": the step-in above the יסוד
"Its border by its edge": the area of the horns at the top

steps.whatToRemember: This answer moves the five-handbreadth cubits from the height to the insets (יסוד, סובב, קרנות). It solves the עולת העוף problem, but it is not the last word: steps 10-19 attack it, and step 20 gives a different reading.

phrases.english: Rather, "the bottom a cubit" means an inset,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 43:13. The wall steps in one cubit above the יסוד.

phrases.english: "a cubit wide" means an inset,
"its border by its edge all around" means an inset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by replacing the height reading of step 3 with a width reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrases measure heights of the מזבח in five-handbreadth cubits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrases measure the one-cubit insets at the יסוד, the סובב, and the horns.

steps.title: With the new reading, the numbers work out
steps.stepSummary: With all the height in six-handbreadth cubits, the מזבח is 60 handbreadths tall. The סובב sits 6 handbreadths above the middle, so one cubit below it still does not fall into the lower half.
steps.simpleTranslation: How tall is the מזבח? Sixty handbreadths. How much is half the מזבח? Thirty. How much is it from the horns down to the סובב? Twenty-four. So how much short of the middle of the מזבח is the סובב? Six. And we learned: if he did it below his feet, even one cubit, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalculates the height of the מזבח using the new reading from Step 7. It shows that the problem with the עולת העוף is now gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the five-handbreadth cubits now measure only the insets, all ten cubits of height are six handbreadths each, which makes 60. The middle is at 30, and the סובב is 24 below the top, so it is 6 handbreadths above the middle. One cubit (6 handbreadths) below the כהן's feet reaches the middle line but does not drop below it, so the ברייתא works.

keyTerms.meaning: its half (the halfway point)
less than, short of
the horns at the top corners of the מזבח
the ledge running around the מזבח, where the כהן walks

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this 60 with the 54 from Step 5. The 54 came from the old reading, where six of the height cubits were only five handbreadths. Here all ten height cubits are full six-handbreadth cubits.

phrases.english: How much is the altar? Sixty.
phrases.notes: He means sixty handbreadths tall: ten cubits of six handbreadths each.

phrases.english: How much is half of the altar? Thirty.

phrases.aramaic: מִקְּרָנוֹת וְעַד סוֹבֵב כַּמָּה הָוֵי? עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבְּעָה.
phrases.english: How much is it from the horns until the ledge? Twenty-four.
By how much is it short of half the altar? Six.
phrases.notes: So the סובב sits 6 handbreadths above the middle, not 3 as in Step 5.

phrases.english: And we learned: if he did it below his feet,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא about squeezing the blood of the עולת העוף, from Step 6.

phrases.english: even one cubit, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It finishes the answer from Step 7 by showing that the math now fits the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The five-handbreadth cubits were part of the height, so the סובב was too close to the middle line.
steps.terutzMaskana: The height is fully in six-handbreadth cubits. The סובב is 6 handbreadths above the middle, so one cubit below it stays in the upper half.

steps.title: Restating the new reading before testing it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up: we explained the פסוק as describing the insets.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain it? As referring to the inset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא briefly restates its new reading. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added here. The question-and-answer simply locks in the claim, the five-handbreadth cubits are the insets, so it can be tested against a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: you explained it as (you set it up as referring to)
inset, where the wall of the מזבח steps inward

phrases.english: How did you explain it? As the inset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It restates the answer from Step 7 so the next challenge can target it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did we say the five-handbreadth cubits refer to?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To the insets of the מזבח.

steps.title: The משנה says the second level is exactly 30 by 30
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in מדות says the מזבח was 32 by 32, stepped in one cubit at the יסוד, and so was 30 by 30. With five-handbreadth insets, it should be 30 cubits and 2 handbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can you really explain it as the inset? Didn't we learn: The מזבח was thirty-two by thirty-two. It rose a cubit and stepped in a cubit, and that is the יסוד. So it comes out thirty by thirty. But it would be thirty cubits and two handbreadths!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading using the משנה that lists the widths of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses round numbers: 32 cubits wide, minus a one-cubit inset on each side, leaves 30. If each inset were only a five-handbreadth cubit, 2 handbreadths fewer would be removed in total. Then the next level would be 30 cubits and 2 handbreadths, not a clean 30.

keyTerms.meaning: can you really explain it this way?
the base, the bottom level of the מזבח
it comes out, it turns out
stepped inward

phrases.english: And can you explain it as the inset?
But didn't we learn: the altar was
thirty-two by thirty-two cubits,

phrases.aramaic: עָלָה אַמָּה וְכָנַס אַמָּה – זֶהוּ יְסוֹד,
phrases.english: it rose a cubit and stepped in a cubit; this is the base,
so it comes out thirty by thirty.
It would be thirty cubits and two handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לָהּ בִּכְנִיסָה? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It attacks the reading that Step 9 just restated.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the five-handbreadth cubits are the insets.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives round-number widths (30 by 30). Short insets would leave an extra 2 handbreadths.

steps.title: The סובב level should be 28 cubits and 4 handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה continues: after another one-cubit inset at the סובב, the מזבח is 28 by 28. With short insets, it would be 28 cubits and 4 handbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: And further: it rose five and stepped in a cubit, and that is the סובב. So it comes out twenty-eight by twenty-eight. But it would be twenty-eight cubits and four handbreadths!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger version of the same challenge from the next line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the סובב, a second short inset leaves another 2 extra handbreadths. Now the gap from the משנה's round number is 4 handbreadths. The new reading clashes with the משנה twice, and the error grows with each level.

keyTerms.meaning: and furthermore (adding another problem)

steps.whatToRemember: The reading that says the five-handbreadth cubits are the insets solves the עולת העוף problem. But it clashes with the round-number widths in the משנה in מדות: 30 by 30 and 28 by 28.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ: עָלָה חָמֵשׁ, וְכָנַס אַמָּה – זֶהוּ סוֹבֵב.
phrases.english: And further: it rose five and stepped in a cubit; this is the ledge.
phrases.notes: "Rose five" means five more cubits above the base.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה עַל עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה.
phrases.english: So it comes out twenty-eight by twenty-eight.
It would be twenty-eight cubits and four handbreadths!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected spelling. Same meaning either way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It extends the challenge of Step 10 to the next level of the מזבח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the five-handbreadth cubits are the insets.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second short inset makes the extra amount 4 handbreadths. That contradicts the משנה's 28 by 28.

steps.title: The corners make the leftover handbreadths add up to a full cubit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא heads off an easy answer (the משנה ignores amounts smaller than a cubit) by quoting the next part of the משנה: after the corners, the top is 26 by 26.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: since the extra is not a full cubit, the משנה did not count it, look at what comes next: 'The place of the horns, a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, so it comes out 26 by 26.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible answer to the last question. It brings the next line of the משנה, about the corners of the מזבח, to set up a bigger problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could say the 2 or 4 extra handbreadths from Steps 10-11 were just too small to mention. But the corners are a third inset. With five-handbreadth insets, the total extra is now 6 handbreadths, which is a full cubit, and a full cubit cannot be ignored.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say: the גמרא raises a possible answer so it can knock it down
He does not count it
The space taken up by the horns (corners) of the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הָוֵי אַמָּה,
phrases.english: And if you would say: since it is not a full cubit,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the few extra handbreadths left over from the short insets in Steps 10-11.

phrases.english: the משנה does not count it,
[but the משנה continues:] The place of the horns:
a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא עֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ עַל עֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ.
phrases.english: so it comes out twenty-six by twenty-six.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הָוֵי אַמָּה, לָא חָשֵׁיב לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible defense against the קשיא of Steps 10-11 and brings the next clause of the משנה to set up a stronger question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה simply leaves out amounts smaller than a cubit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three short insets add up to six handbreadths, a full cubit, so the gap can no longer be brushed off as too small.

steps.title: It should be twenty-seven
steps.stepSummary: With five-handbreadth insets, the top of the מזבח would be 27 by 27, not 26 by 26.
steps.simpleTranslation: It would be twenty-seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the problem outright: using short insets, the משנה's number of 26 is off by a whole cubit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each inset of 5 handbreadths instead of 6 leaves one extra handbreadth on each side, so two extra per measurement. Three insets leave 6 extra handbreadths, one full cubit. The משנה's count of 32 minus 2, minus 2, minus 2 gives 26, but with short insets the real width would be one cubit more: 27.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-seven (in Aramaic)

phrases.english: It would be twenty-seven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge set up in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the insets were measured in five-handbreadth cubits
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The math of short insets gives 27 by 27, but the משנה says 26 by 26.

steps.title: The משנה was not exact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא did not give a precise number.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was not precise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה was rounding and did not bother with exact numbers here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer keeps the five-handbreadth insets. It says 26 is not an exact number, so it does not prove that the insets were full six-handbreadth cubits.

keyTerms.meaning: He was not exact: the תנא gave an approximate number

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not precise' here means the משנה said 26 when the truth was 27. That is a full cubit off, not a tiny rounding. That is why the גמרא will soon test whether this answer can really hold.

phrases.english: He was not precise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The source's number is approximate (לא דק)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The number 26 is exact, so the insets must be full cubits
steps.terutzMaskana: 26 is a loose number; the real measurement could be 27

steps.title: The wood area should then be twenty-five
steps.stepSummary: The משנה goes on: subtract a cubit on each side for the priests' walkway, leaving 24 by 24 for the wood. If the top were really 27, the wood area would be 25.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The place where the כהנים walk is a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, so 24 by 24 is left for the מערכה.' But it would be twenty-five!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the משנה and shows that the same problem comes back with the next number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the top was really 27 by 27, taking off a cubit on each side for the walkway leaves 25 by 25. The משנה says 24 by 24. So the short-inset idea is off by a cubit again.

keyTerms.meaning: The strip on top of the מזבח where the כהנים walked
The area where the wood pile for the fire was arranged

phrases.english: The place where the feet of the כהנים walk,
a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע עַל עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע
phrases.english: So it comes out twenty-four by twenty-four
as the place of the wood arrangement.
It would be twenty-five!
phrases.notes: Now the גמרא is speaking again: 27 minus a cubit on each side is 25.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new number from the same משנה, so the problem comes back even after the לא דק answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The five-handbreadth insets, still being defended by 'not precise'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wood area would be 25 by 25, but the משנה says 24 by 24.

steps.title: A פסוק confirms that 24 is exact
steps.stepSummary: One cannot say 'not precise' again, because a פסוק in יחזקאל teaches that the wood area measures exactly twelve cubits from the middle in every direction, which is 24 by 24.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say here too he was not precise, but it is written: 'And the hearth is twelve long by twelve wide, square.' One might think it is only twelve by twelve. When it says 'on its four sides,' it teaches that one measures twelve cubits from the middle in each direction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the 'not precise' answer for the number 24. It shows from a פסוק that 24 by 24 is an exact measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אריאל is the place of the fire, the wood area. The words 'on its four sides' teach that the twelve cubits are measured from the center out to each side, so the whole area is 24 by 24. Since a פסוק gives this number, it is exact, and the short insets that would make it 25 run into a strong problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The hearth: the fire area on top of the מזבח where the wood was arranged
But it is written: brings a פסוק as a challenge
Square
In each and every direction

steps.whatToRemember: Three short insets would make the top of the מזבח one cubit wider than the משנה says. 'Not precise' might cover the 26, but it cannot cover the 24, because the פסוק in יחזקאל gives 24 by 24 exactly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the challenge from 'the משנה rounded' into 'a פסוק contradicts you,' which puts heavy pressure on the idea that the insets were five-handbreadth cubits.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי לָא דָּק,
phrases.english: And if you would say: here too he was not precise,
but isn't it written:
"And the hearth shall be twelve long
by twelve wide, square";
one might think that it is only
twelve by twelve;
when it says: "on its four sides,"
it teaches that from the middle one measures

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ וָרוּחַ.
phrases.english: twelve cubits in each and every direction.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי לָא דָּק, וְהָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects using the לא דק answer of Step 14 for the new number in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'not precise' to explain the 24 by 24 wood area
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק fixes the wood area at exactly 24 by 24, so the number cannot be approximate. Short insets, which give 25, clash with the פסוק.

steps.title: Maybe six of the base's cubits were short cubits
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest that six of the 32 cubits of the מזבח's base were measured with small cubits of five handbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: six of those cubits were counted from the start as cubits of five handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible answer to the problem from the last steps: maybe the משנה counted six of the base's cubits as short five-handbreadth cubits. This only sets up the next move, where the idea will be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The numbers did not work when the insets were short cubits but the base's 32 was counted in full cubits. So the suggestion is that the 32 cubits of the base were not all the same size. If six of them were one handbreadth shorter, the whole base shrinks by six handbreadths, which is one full cubit, and the top numbers in the משנה would fit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you would say': brings up a possible answer, usually so it can be rejected
A short cubit of five handbreadths, instead of the normal six
From the start, from the beginning
Six of them, meaning six of the 32 cubits

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the whole מזבח was measured in short cubits. The suggestion is that only six of the 32 cubits were short.

phrases.english: And if you would say: six of them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the 32 cubits of the base of the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: מֵעִיקָּרָא בְּאַמָּה בַּת חַמְשָׁה מַיְיתֵי לְהוּ,
phrases.english: from the start, he counts them as cubits of five handbreadths,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: שֵׁית מִינַּיְיהוּ מֵעִיקָּרָא בְּאַמָּה בַּת חַמְשָׁה מַיְיתֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new way to save the numbers after step 16 ruled out saying the numbers were 'not precise'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the size of the measuring unit for part of the base
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All 32 cubits of the base are full six-handbreadth cubits, so the numbers don't add up.
steps.terutzMaskana: If six of the cubits were five handbreadths each, the base is one cubit smaller and the top measurements might fit.

steps.title: Then the courtyard would have an extra cubit
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails, because a smaller מזבח would leave an extra, unexplained cubit of space in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the courtyard would have extra space.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the short-cubit idea. If the base were really one cubit smaller, the courtyard's total length would not be fully used up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six short cubits make the base 31 normal cubits instead of 32. The courtyard has a fixed total length, and every part of it is listed. Taking a cubit away from the מזבח leaves one cubit that no listed area covers. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces the problem that follows from an idea
Has extra room, is too wide
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: If so – the courtyard has extra space.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea that six of the base's cubits were short cubits
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It makes the מזבח 31 cubits long, which leaves one cubit of the עזרה unaccounted for.

steps.title: The courtyard's measurements add up exactly with a 32-cubit מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in מסכת מדות listing every part of the עזרה from east to west, and it totals exactly 187 cubits only if the מזבח is a full 32.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: The whole courtyard was 187 cubits long and 135 cubits wide. From east to west it was 187: the area where Israelites could walk was 11 cubits, the area where כהנים could walk was 11 cubits, the מזבח was 32, between the אולם and the מזבח was 22 cubits, the היכל was 100 cubits, and there were 11 cubits behind the בית הכפורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind step 18. It lists each section of the courtyard's length so we can add them up ourselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Add the sections: 11 + 11 + 32 + 22 + 100 + 11 = 187, exactly the total length. If the מזבח were only 31, the parts would add up to 186, one cubit short of 187. That proves the מזבח's base was a full 32 normal cubits.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where feet may step: the area people were allowed to walk in
The entrance hall in front of the היכל
The main building of the בית המקדש (the Sanctuary)
The room of the ark cover: the קדש הקדשים

steps.whatToRemember: The courtyard's parts add up to exactly 187 cubits only if the מזבח is a full 32 cubits. So the base cannot be one cubit smaller.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: the entire courtyard was
187 cubits long
by 135 cubits wide,
from east to west, 187:

phrases.aramaic: מְקוֹם דְּרִיסַת רַגְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל – אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה,
phrases.english: the area where Israelites set their feet – eleven cubits,

phrases.aramaic: וּמְקוֹם דְּרִיסַת רַגְלֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים – אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה,
phrases.english: and the area where the priests set their feet – eleven cubits,
the altar – thirty-two,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין אוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ – עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם אַמָּה,
phrases.english: between the Entrance Hall and the altar – twenty-two cubits,
the Sanctuary – one hundred cubits,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכַּפּוֹרֶת.
phrases.english: eleven cubits behind the Hall of the Ark Cover.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: כׇּל הָעֲזָרָה הָיְתָה אוֹרֶךְ מֵאָה וּשְׁמוֹנִים וָשֶׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that proves the rejection in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That the מזבח's base is a full 32 normal cubits, so six of its cubits cannot be short ones
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת מדות listing the east-to-west parts of the עזרה, which total exactly 187

steps.title: A new reading of the words in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier approach and starts reading the phrases of the פסוק in יחזקאל differently: 'חיק האמה' is the height of the base, and 'אמה רחב' is the inset of the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'the bottom shall be a cubit' – that is its height; 'a cubit wide' – that is the inset; 'its border by its edge round about' –
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier explanation failed, so the גמרא starts a new reading of the פסוק. Each phrase is matched to a different part of the מזבח, and the explanation continues past the end of this passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading says 'חיק האמה' describes the base's height of one cubit, not a width. 'אמה רחב' is the one-cubit inset, where the wall steps in. The meaning of 'גבולה אל שפתה סביב' comes right after this passage ends.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the previous approach and gives a new one
'The bottom of a cubit': a phrase in the פסוק describing the base of the מזבח
Inset: where the wall of the מזבח steps inward
'Its border by its edge': another phrase from the same פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle. The explanation of 'גבולה אל שפתה סביב' is given in the text that follows.

phrases.english: Rather, 'the bottom shall be a cubit' – refers to its height,
'a cubit wide' – refers to the inset,
'its border by its edge round about' –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the short-cubit idea is rejected in steps 18 and 19, the גמרא starts a new way of reading the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the phrases of the פסוק differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrases of the פסוק were read so that the numbers did not fit the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each phrase describes a different part: height, inset, and border. The full reading continues in the next lines.
